sources.entry: WindowCycle - A focused macOS current-app window switcher with a visible panel.

summary.one_liner: WindowCycle is a prototype macOS switcher that cycles through the windows of the frontmost app using Cmd+` (and Cmd+Shift+` backward) and shows them in a visible panel.
summary.what_it_does: WindowCycle registers a Carbon global hotkey so Cmd+` starts a switching session for the current frontmost app and cycles forward through its windows, with Cmd+Shift+` cycling backward. A floating AppKit NSPanel with SwiftUI content displays the window list while the session is active. Releasing Command activates the selected window via AXRaise when the event tap is available, and Escape hides the switcher. Window enumeration uses Accessibility APIs, reading app names, titles, frames, and minimized state. A menu bar status item offers Show, Hide, and Quit actions. The README describes it as a prototype using public APIs only.
use_cases: switch between windows of the same app on macOS
replace Cmd+` window cycling with a visible panel
menu bar app for raising app windows
how_to_run: open Package.swift  (run the WindowCycle executable target in Xcode)
notable: Cmd+` and Cmd+Shift+` cycle windows of the current frontmost app only
Uses public macOS APIs first (Carbon hotkeys, AX, CGEvent tap) rather than private CGS/SLS APIs
Runs as a menu bar agent (LSUIElement) with no Dock icon
Build scripts for local .app bundle, install to /Applications, and release DMG
caveats: Prototype; README says it is not a finished product and has no settings UI
Requires Accessibility permission, and Input Monitoring may be needed for arrow/Escape handling
Cross-Space and full-screen windows are not handled; window order is AX order, not z-order
Current DMG is self-signed and not notarized, so macOS Gatekeeper may block the first launch
